newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean car exports seen rising despite Kia woes.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean car exports seen rising despite Kia woes.

text.p: South Korea's domestic sales and exports of cars rose sharply in July, provisional figures showed on Tuesday, and analysts said they expected improved exports this year despite a crisis at Kia Motors Corp.
Domestic vehicle sales rose to 161,634 in July from 133,591 a year earlier, provisional figures from the Korea Automobile Manufacturers' Association showed.
Vehicle exports totalled a provisional 100,300 in July, up 37 percent from 73,220 a year earlier.
The association raised its export forecast to 1.38 million vehicles this year against an earlier projection of 1.35 million and 1.21 million exported last year.
Analysts said they were optimistic about vehicle exports for the whole of this year, aided by automakers' efforts to diversify their overseas market and introduce new models.
"Korean carmakers will try to push forward with active car exports to offset sluggish domestic sales," said Soh Jong-won, auto analyst at Ssangyong Securities.
Kia's domestic sales totalled 45,222 vehicles in July from 38,556 a year earlier, the association said. Its exports rose to 31,990 from 22,964 a year earlier.
Song Sang-hoon, association research analyst, said Kia's domestic car sales shot up after the troubled company announced deep cash discounts.

Kia Motor Sales Co, sales affiliate of the nation's eighth ranked conglomerate, began selling passenger and commercial vehicles at a 29.9 percent cash discount on July 20 to raise funds. The offer helped Kia raise an estimated 350 billion won ($393.1 million) in cash in three days.
Kia Group, with an estimated 9.5 trillion won in debts, was put under the protection of its creditor banks on July 15 after they determined it would be unable to meet its debt payments.
Kang Hun-sok, auto analyst at ING-Barings, said the July report was expected.
"Kia's increase in sales stems from the discounts offered on its cars in the domestic market, and Daewoo's sales were boosted by aggressive marketing and popular new models," he said.
Daewoo Motor's July vehicle sales jumped to 37,253 in the local market from 15,909 in July last year and to 22,881 units abroad against 7,876.
Suh Sung-moon, auto analyst at Daewoo Securities, said July's brisk car sales were a temporary phenomenon.
"Kia will not be able to sell its cars again at a deep discount. And buyers tend to shy away from products by a troubled company," Suh said.
Ssangyong's Soh predicted a price war among the three leading automakers.
"Kia has no choice but to sell its products at a discount to raise money," Soh said.
He said Hyundai Motor and Daewoo had tolerated the market distortion caused by Kia's discount sales in order to prevent a possible takeover bid by Samsung.
"But they will follow Kia's suit in the long run, worsening their profitability. It'll be a vicious circle," he said.

South Korea's largest carmaker Hyundai Motor sold 59,418 vehicles at home in July, up 3.4 percent from 57,479 a year earlier. It exported 37,523 vehicles, down from 39,118. ($ = 890.4 South Korean Won)
